package_info.package_manager: Windows DLL (PE file, not a traditional package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (multiple trojanized builds, see IOCs for hashes)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is a trojanized version of the legitimate sqlite3.dll, modified to include malicious code for persistence, data exfiltration, and anti-forensics. It is used as a loader for further payloads and is part of a sophisticated APT campaign (Operation CuckooBees) attributed to APT41.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when DLL is loaded via rundll32.exe or by a parent process)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At DLL load-time, the code decrypts an embedded or downloaded payload using AES or ChaCha20, then executes the payload in memory, enabling further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate sqlite3.dll should not contain code to decrypt and execute additional payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A standard DLL should only provide its documented API, not act as a loader for encrypted code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom plugin frameworks may decrypt plugins, but not in a system DLL context.
key_indicators: Use of cryptographic routines (AES, ChaCha20) in a database library

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After payload execution, the code overwrites the contents of the dropped DLL file with random data and then deletes the file, erasing forensic evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate DLLs do not self-delete or overwrite themselves after use.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal DLLs remain static and do not perform anti-forensics.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Self-deleting installers or updaters, but not DLLs loaded by other processes.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when DLL is loaded with specific export function via rundll32.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a specific export function is called (e.g., via rundll32.exe with a third parameter), the code collects system information and sends it to a command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exported functions in sqlite3.dll should not collect or exfiltrate system information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLL exports are for database operations, not system reconnaissance or C2 communication.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Diagnostic tools may collect system info, but not in a database DLL context.

attack_chain.action: Initial infection: Malicious sqlite3.dll is dropped onto the target system, replacing or supplementing the legitimate DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: DLL is loaded by a legitimate or attacker-controlled process.

attack_chain.action: DLL load: The trojanized DLL is loaded (e.g., via rundll32.exe or a parent application), triggering malicious code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decryption and execution of embedded or downloaded payload.

attack_chain.action: Payload execution: Decrypted payload is run in memory, enabling further malicious actions (e.g., data theft, lateral movement).
attack_chain.leads_to: System information collection and C2 communication.

attack_chain.action: Anti-forensics: The malicious DLL overwrites its own contents with random data and deletes itself to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Removal of forensic evidence and persistence of only in-memory artifacts.

behavioral_signatures: DLLs (especially sqlite3.dll) performing cryptographic decryption and in-memory code execution
DLLs overwriting and deleting themselves after execution
Non-standard export functions in system or third-party DLLs
DLLs loaded via rundll32.exe with unusual parameters
file_indicators: sqlite3.dll with unexpected hash (see provided SHA256 IOCs)
Presence of DLLs in unusual directories or replacing legitimate system files
DLLs that are deleted shortly after being loaded
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure (as identified in threat intelligence feeds)
Unexpected network activity from processes loading sqlite3.dll
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLL files named sqlite3.dll with hashes matching known IOCs. Alert on DLLs that perform cryptographic operations or spawn network connections. Detect DLLs that overwrite and delete themselves after execution. Monitor for rundll32.exe loading sqlite3.dll with non-standard export functions or parameters. Correlate with network traffic to known C2 domains or IPs.
